Forgery
FOR-jer-ee
n. (the crime of counterfeiting a writing, a name, or a coin; also the false thing itself)
From forge, originally to work metal into shape. Webster notes that sense as rare. The living sense is the crime of counterfeiting: a writing, a name, a note, or a coin, to the prejudice of another. Also the counterfeit thing itself.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain. Paul warns the Thessalonians not to be shaken by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us. John closes the book with a testimony against any man who adds to the words of the prophecy.

Forgery is a false making offered as a true one. A counterfeit coin, a false name on a bond, a letter that pretends to be Paul's, a pen that pretends to be the law of the LORD — the instrument changes. The sin is the same. Something is made to pass for what it is not, and another man bears the loss.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): the crime of counterfeiting, as of coin, notes, or a bond; also the counterfeit thing itself. Forgery may consist in counterfeiting a writing, or in setting a false name to it.

expand to see more

FORGERY, n. The crime of counterfeiting; as the forgery of coin, or of bank notes, or of a bond.

Forgery may consist in counterfeiting a writing, or in setting a false name to it, to the prejudice of another person.

That which is forged or counterfeited.

Key Scripture

Jer 8:8 — "How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain."

2Th 2:2 — "That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand."

Rev 22:18 — "For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book:"

Modern Corruption

The age multiplies false makings and calls them content, so that a counterfeit voice, letter, or image passes until someone else pays for it.

expand to see more

Webster's prejudice-of-another-person is the moral core the age drops. A forged note is not a clever craft. It is a writing made to injure the man whose name or goods it counterfeits.

The same sin reaches the Scriptures when a pen pretends the law of the LORD is still in the hand that has already made the pen vain. Adding to the prophecy is not editing. It is forgery against the Author.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

No single biblical headword. The field is a vain pen (Jer 8:8), a letter as from us (2Th 2:2), and adding to the prophecy (Rev 22:18).

expand to see more

The old sense, working metal, is why the word still sounds like a shop. The crime is a shop that stamps a false name.

Second Thessalonians 2:2 assumes forgeries of Paul were already in circulation. The church was told not to be shaken by them.

Usage

"Nor by letter as from us — a forged apostolic hand."

"The pen of the scribes is in vain — a forgery that still quotes the law."
